correctness.rationale: The two-phase variance-process stationary flux exactly yields the size-biased beta density with normalization \(\bar v\), not an ordinary beta. Conditional independent Gaussians give the exact chi-square mixture. Uniform-in-latent-variance Stirling expansion yields conditional rate \(I(s\mid v)=(s/v-1-\log(s/v))/2\); its strict minimizer lies at \(a\), \(s\), or \(b\) according to the three regions. One-sided Watson formulas give both gamma factors and polynomial powers. Substitution \(v=a+y/\sqrt N\) or \(v=b-y/\sqrt N\), with Gaussian domination, yields the two locally uniform critical profiles and their exact edge limits. A second endpoint integration gives threshold probability slopes. The reproducibility checker passed 40 finite-parameter numerical diagnostics in two distinct endpoint regimes; analytic derivation proves the universal conclusions.

value.rationale: For a natural stationary collective observable, generic weak convergence says nothing about the exponentially small energy probability outside the latent-variance interval. The new formulas supply the sharp rare-event probabilities and a finite-size edge theory rather than another stationary moment. Separate powers \(N^{1/2-p}\) and \(N^{1/2-q}\) carry the two switching-rate signatures even though their exponential rates are rate-independent; threshold \(p=1\) and \(q=1\) identifies a measurable contrast between divergent and depleted finite-size energy-edge peaks. The exact constants are needed for tail calibration and distinguish the result from repackaging the already published weak-limit law.
